title: 🏛️ Exam 2024 technical · reading: a woman car mechanic ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 1)
A text tells the story of Caroline Smith, who works with cars.

A suitable title for the text can be:
questions.explanation: The text follows Caroline from her love of cars to her work as a mechanic and her own business, where she trains women and men. A title about a female mechanic covers all of it: "young" is the exam's wording, and "female mechanic" is the part the text proves. Selling cars and training as an apprentice are two early steps of her career, true details that cannot be the title of the whole text.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 2a, paragraph 2)
Caroline Smith passed an exam and worked in several garages before opening her business. Is the statement below true or false, going by paragraph 2?

"Caroline enjoyed her work in all the garages."
questions.explanation: The statement is false: a sentence of paragraph 2 says the opposite. Judge a statement by the words of the paragraph, not by what seems likely.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 2a, paragraph 2)
A student says: "Caroline enjoyed her work in all the garages." Which part of paragraph 2 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: took an exam and became a mechanic
she set up her own business
Working in many garages was not a good experience
teaching basic mechanics to hundreds of women and men

questions.explanation: The text says directly that working in many garages was not a good experience for her. Taking the exam, setting up her business and teaching are things she did, not how she felt about her work.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
In the last paragraph, Caroline Smith looks to the future and quotes some customers. Judge the statement below against what it says.

"Caroline wants other women to work as car mechanics."
questions.explanation: The statement is true: a sentence of paragraph 3 says the same in other words. Judge a statement by the words of the paragraph, not by what seems likely.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
A student says: "Caroline wants other women to work as car mechanics." Which part of paragraph 3 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: they wish they had done this when they were younger
where more women can train to be mechanics
they didn't see it as a choice then

questions.explanation: Caroline hopes to have garages where more women can train to be mechanics: she wants more women in the job. The two other parts report what customers say about the past, not what she wants.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 3, paragraphs 1 and 2)
Caroline Smith's story says: "In 1992, I started working for a car company as a seller"; "in 1999, I asked the company's manager to take me on as an … apprentice"; "in 2006, she set up her own business".

Match each event, as the exam table words it, with its date.

options.text: She began taking lessons in mechanics
She built a new car company
She started working as a seller in a car company

questions.explanation: In 1992 she started as a seller. In 1999 she became an apprentice one day a week, which is when she began learning mechanics. In 2006 she set up her own business, the new company in the table.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 4, paragraph 1)
Paragraph 1 says: "As a teenager, I used to read motor magazines."

What does this sentence express?

options.text: a single event that happened once

questions.explanation: As a teenager she read motor magazines regularly, but she does not do it any more: it was a habit in the past. It is not a routine of today, not one event and not a plan for the future.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, technical — reading, question 5, paragraph 1)
Paragraph 1 says: "But in 1999, I asked the company's manager to take me on as an unpaid apprentice one day a week."

Which word from paragraph 1 means nearly the same as "receiving no money"?
questions.explanation: "Unpaid" means receiving no money for the work. The apprentice is the person who learns the job, the seller sells cars and the manager runs the company.
